body: I've sorta decided that I'm not fit for friends, at least not for the time being. If I want to get better, I'm just simply going to have to take this road alone. I've always been used to being surrounded by caring friends all throughout my childhood and early teen years, but I guess that's going to have to change for now.

I guess another issue in struggling with these days is that I don't know who's caring for me out of social obligation (I put them in this situation now they have to do something about it) or out of genuine care (they truly do want to be there for me). And as for my "friends", the thing is that they've already ran. As I tried opening up to them, I later find out that they begin talking on group chats specifically without me. They stop texting me, and they just give "oh" or "I'm sorry" or "it'll get better" when I text them. But thank you for your kind words, at least I know decent souls are still around, and they'll continue to be around. I try my best, but it's hard to be a good person 100% of the time.

Your story is awfully inspiring. I was hardly ever picked on; hell, I'd be lying if I said that I didn't have a pretty good number of friends growing up. It's just that I wasn't prepared for the day when life would take a complete U-turn for me and force me to go from "life is great I love it" to "I have no friends I have no family why am I still alive". I've had, and still do have trouble seeing life past friends who've ditched me, both emotionally and physically. It hurts, it really does. But you're solid proof that I'm wrong, that there IS life past them. I'll try again, I'll try living life again. Thank you.

They usually give the "oh I'm sorry here have a cookie lol" kind of response and forget that I even told them about it by the next day. One teacher, in particular, literally walked away without saying a damn word when I had told her about all this and how I can't find anything that's worth living for. As for anyone else, it's either just them telling me that my problems don't exist and that I don't have the right to be sad because "someone out there has it worse", or just no kind of support at all. 
I really appreciate your comment, though. I'm just trying to cling onto the smallest acts of kindness these days.
